issues.title: Scale ordinary Workspace range COW and Commit from observed shell failures
issues.body:
Follow-up to #243 and parent #232. The user-facing operation is `WorkspaceApi::exec(command)` running ordinary shell/POSIX operations on the mounted Workspace, followed by explicit Commit. This issue tracks an extensible range-based COW upper and a focused first verification phase for failures already observed on that route.

**Many-file closure requirement (2026-09-26):** [#256](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/256) is now an actual subissue of this parent. It owns removal of the 128 dirty-identity/changed-name and 32 KiB prepared-metadata ceilings, directory-local 128 limits, and adjacent runtime/cache or C1 limits reached by ordinary package install/update. [#248](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/248) owns final changed runs within one file. Package-scale closure under #245 requires both public SDK/FUSE gates; completing #248 alone does not prove a many-tiny-file update.

## Current evidence

- #243 Phase 2 mixed package refresh failed when `mv -f package-lock.json.next package-lock.json` returned EIO; Exec exited before Commit. The 4 KiB overwrite and 16 one-byte writes passed functionally, but all latency rows are cache-ineligible and the receipts are not admission-complete.
- #232's retained ordinary POSIX shift diagnostic counted 9 versus 81 FUSE WRITEs, 51 versus 3,363 cumulative old-piece loads, and 10 versus 144 rebuilt index pages at 1 versus 10 MiB. The larger v2 failures observed five-second silent Exec Unknown; an 8 MiB replay violation is a separate source/registry deduction.
- Current per-file bounds include 1,024 pieces, 256 changed intervals, and 8 MiB of final non-base content for an existing file. The Bridge EditFile request repeats the 8 MiB/256 bounds. File-size and real memory/disk budgets remain necessary.
- Future many-package loads also meet distinct namespace bounds: 128 dirty identities, 128 changed names, and a 32 KiB metadata request per generation. Current Commit reconciliation can return Busy if the active generation changes during successor installation; continuous writes during Commit need proof, not an assumed PASS.

## Deliverables

Create `core/docs/issues/245/` with:

1. Architecture for scalable Base/Local/Zero range COW on ordinary FUSE WRITE/SETATTR, path-local index updates, immutable generation capture, bounded payload custody/reclamation, and streaming file/namespace Commit. No shell classifier, special edit tool, or ioctl route.
2. Implementation plan with source ownership, staged gates, format/protocol implications, rollback/uncertain-outcome rules, and resource-based rather than arbitrary piece/replay ceilings.
3. Phase 1 verification plan focused on the existing root rename failure, small-write full-list work, large POSIX shift/progress/capacity location, cleanup overhead, correctness, and cache/receipt eligibility. Preserve historical receipts unchanged; freeze any new scenario before one attempt per case/arm.
4. A separate brainstorm of later load-bearing ordinary shell cases: many packages, one large package, move/remove/copy, large edits, and command output versus Workspace log files. These are future work, not Phase 1 PASS claims.

Keep the first implementation/verification work focused on previously observed failures. The architecture must leave room for larger workloads without claiming they already pass. Follow AGENTS.md, core/AGENTS.md, benchmark rules, and documentation policy. Do not inflate timeouts, workers, or quotas to turn a miss into a pass.

Source references: #243, PR #244, and the retained reports under `core/docs/issues/232/` and `core/docs/issues/243/evidence/phase2-ordinary-shell-v1/`.


## Documentation prepared — 2026-09-25

The five planning files are committed at [`9951a8554`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/commit/9951a855455c1570ead9d26c2dd13c969e35d3b1) on [`codex/issue245-range-cow-plan`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/tree/codex/issue245-range-cow-plan) and available for review in draft [PR #246](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/pull/246). The current issue folder is [`core/docs/issues/245/`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/tree/d63379b955d1af4656cbfe23ebefc05ebf36ef8c/core/docs/issues/245). It contains the architecture, implementation plan, Phase 1 verification, deferred load-bearing brainstorm, and README.

Three independent subagent research passes covered the product/Commit source, retained Phase 1 evidence, and future workload limits before drafting. The docs preserve the observed-versus-inferred failure distinction and state that continuous Commit reconciliation remains unproven. Local Markdown links, policy status banners and staged whitespace passed checks. Production LOC remained 120780 -> 120780 (delta +0; reference 65417, Core 55363). No product code changed and no benchmark arm was sampled. #245 stays open for implementation and verification.


## Architecture clarification — 2026-09-25

[Commit `fd77f5b47`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/commit/fd77f5b47) updates the planning docs with the proposed dynamic-height B+ tree-style sequence, local private-backing placement, and a two-sequential-Commit G1 → G2 → G3 timeline. Successful Commit reconciliation while later POSIX writes continue remains an explicit unproven gate. The update changes only docs; production LOC remains 120780 -> 120780 (delta +0).


## Phase 1 implementation handoff — 2026-09-25

[Commit `d63379b95`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/commit/d63379b955d1af4656cbfe23ebefc05ebf36ef8c) adds the copyable [handoff prompt](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d63379b955d1af4656cbfe23ebefc05ebf36ef8c/core/docs/issues/245/HANDOFF_PHASE1_PROMPT.md). It gives the implementing agent required reading, before/after architecture, provisional file layout and LOC estimate, complexity bounds, command-agnostic FUSE route, and the focused Phase 1 proof. It is planning only; no implementation or benchmark sample was run.

## Architecture and complexity research — 2026-09-26

The [source-pinned research commit `7939c56d1`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/commit/7939c56d1) is reviewable in draft [PR #250](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/pull/250), stacked on the #245 implementation branch. Its [architecture map](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7939c56d1/core/docs/issues/245/ARCHITECTURE_COMPLEXITY_RESEARCH.md), [private backing/page-tree audit](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7939c56d1/core/docs/issues/245/PRIVATE_BACKING_AND_PAGE_TREE.md), and [Commit-time final-delta algorithm](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7939c56d1/core/docs/issues/245/FINAL_DELTA_COMMIT_COMPLEXITY.md) provide diagrams, comparison tables, asymptotic costs, resource accounting, and deterministic proof gates.

At final product source `b2cd0df23`, the strict E mounted-write-during-builder-read gate and F's frozen comparative wall envelope are PASS; every F latency cell remains INELIGIBLE. The original issue body's 1,024/256/8 MiB limits describe its pre-A–F baseline. The current remaining 4,096 final-run path is [#248](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/248); multiple concurrent SDK Exec calls and mounts follow in [#249](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/249).

The source audit exposes three extra gates before the optimized architecture can be claimed: an independent 4,096-live-payload-record cap; a source-derived risk at the 249/250-leaf height transition and narrow height-2 splice, pending a reproducer; and repeated ancestor reads during sequential cursor traversal (`O(H×L)` page visits versus the target amortized `O(H+L)`). C1's replay interface and exact canonical-root compatibility are separate #248 proof obligations. No product code or benchmark arm changed in this research commit. Production LOC: 125398 -> 125398 (delta +0; Core 56670, legacy 68728).

## Commit write-progress qualification — 2026-09-26

The [phase audit at `3b7917e60`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/3b7917e60/core/docs/issues/245/ARCHITECTURE_COMPLEXITY_RESEARCH.md#what-writes-continue-during-commit-currently-proves) narrows “non-pausing” to what the E receipt actually proved: a mounted write was accepted while a successor-builder page **read** was held, and a second sequential Commit preserved both heads. It is not a claim that every mounted write completes immediately throughout Commit. Current `lower_file` holds the shared metadata writer through a whole frozen-file extent walk; `ReplacementSource::pull` reacquires it per transfer pull. A mounted mutation can wait for these holds until its own deadline. A held builder page write with an unfinished slot remains a separate, correctly refused schedule. Independent SDK Exec and Commit controls are also serialized by the current daemon (#249).

For #248, include a phase-by-phase liveness gate: freeze G1; barrier writes during lowering, descriptor emission, replacement transfer, remote construction and reconciliation; report accepted/rejected writes, maximum writer-gate hold/wait, backing-window owner, deadline outcome, live revision, and exact old/new heads. The target holds no mutation gate for work proportional to extents, final runs, replacement bytes or remote I/O. Explicit capacity, deadlines and unresolved custody still apply. This is source-backed design work; no new timed sample or product change was made.

## Animated incremental Commit walkthrough — 2026-09-26

The ten-frame GIF in research commit 9c6316403 shows five lanes: shell/FUSE, active Workspace root, private backing pages and payloads, frozen Commit root, and Store head. It follows C0 -> frozen G1 -> live G2 -> C1 -> C2, including the post-capture payload Y and its reanchoring after C1. The animation is a version-isolation explanation, not a claim that every current Commit phase is pause-free.

![Incremental Commit showing frozen and live Workspace roots over private backing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/9c631640329c9a21e0e151c131c5e38df8902ffd/core/docs/issues/245/assets/incremental-commit-private-backing.gif)

[Read the accompanying architecture and phase qualifications](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/9c631640329c9a21e0e151c131c5e38df8902ffd/core/docs/issues/245/ARCHITECTURE_COMPLEXITY_RESEARCH.md).

issues.title: Stream final file deltas at Commit without a fixed edit-run limit
issues.body:
Parent: #245.

**Current-source update after #252 (2026-09-26):** The prerequisite generic file-save cutover is in `main` through PR #253. Current production uses `SaveFile` opcode 20 with one frozen final `Base`/`Local`/`Zero` stream; `EditFile`, `ConstructFile`, the old Begin descriptor route, direct Workspace range entrypoints and the FUSE ioctl callback have been removed. The source diagrams and code links below describe their historical pinned revisions. For new work on this issue, preserve the current generic route and prove larger-run scaling, amortized cursor traversal, bounded resources, writer progress across Commit phases and incremental-head correctness. The owner accepted 1,024 separated runs for #252 and directed no further 4,097 rerun in that sub-issue; #248's independent larger-scale gate remains open.

**Public API benchmark requirement (owner direction, 2026-09-26):** The 4,097-separated-final-run timed gate must enter through public `WorkspaceApi::mount` → `WorkspaceApi::exec` → `WorkspaceApi::commit`. The Exec command runs ordinary file syscalls against the mounted Workspace path (for example, one shell-launched program performing 4,097 positional writes); the measured driver must not call `Workspace::own_payload`, `Workspace::write_file`, FUSE callbacks, Bridge, service, or C1 directly to create the changes. Those internal calls made by the product behind the public API remain part of the measured work. Record Exec, Commit, and cleanup wall separately, plus the complete-command budget and cache contract. The retained #252 4,097 diagnostics and 1,024 pass used native existing-file handles, with no mounted/FUSE writes; they are useful diagnostics, not this public API benchmark. Internal count-driven probes may diagnose the cost but must be labeled separately from the API gate. Current source imposes a 30,000 ms whole-Exec deadline (`WORKSPACE_EXEC_MAX_MS`) and kills the shell process group when it expires. Owner direction (2026-09-26) is to remove this product runtime ceiling; #249 owns the control-protocol, daemon, and SDK change. Record Exec wall, and keep the 60 s functional harness ceiling and the repository performance budget as measurement gates; neither is a product command-kill timer. Do not change the 4,097-write workload to make a row fit. A normal performance-selection admission also needs its own repository budget and cache-qualified receipt.

**Namespace-cardinality sibling:** [#256](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/256) removes the separate 128 dirty-identity/changed-name and 32 KiB prepared-metadata ceilings for many-tiny-file package updates. This issue's 4,097 final runs belong to one dirty file, so passing #248 does not satisfy #256; both are required for #245's package-scale claim.

## Execution plan on the current `SaveFile` source (2026-09-26)

The historical design and source links below predate #252. Its streaming `SaveFile` route, separate stream-byte budget and removal of the 4,096 payload-record admission cap are already on `main`; verify the current source before implementing any older step.

1. **Freeze the public workload and evidence contract.** Prepare one closed existing-file master, then use an independent writable copy per run. The measured driver uses only public `WorkspaceApi::mount`, one `WorkspaceApi::exec` that launches one writer process issuing exactly 4,097 separated positional file writes through the mount, and `WorkspaceApi::commit`. Record the actual FUSE-write count, final changed-run count, Exec, Commit, complete command and cleanup. Verify exact new bytes and the old head independently through public access. Record Exec wall and retain the 60 s functional harness ceiling; the whole-Exec product timeout is removed under #249. A performance selection has the repository's separate complete-command limit of 15 s by default, or a 25 s exception declared before its one sample; its cache state must be controlled and recorded. A timed-out or cache-ineligible row remains nonpassing.
2. **Diagnose the public path early, without using a performance rerun.** Reuse #252's native receipts as diagnostics. Run one labeled, count-driven API diagnostic at a smaller fixed write count with checkpoints, plus a same-range overwrite control if needed. Count FUSE callbacks, payload records examined by routine cleanup, page-file creates/allocations, ownership-ledger reads/writes, extent-tree page visits, root publications, and time by acquisition/publication. Use external tracing or legitimate production telemetry, not a benchmark driver that calls internal mutation methods or test-only product hooks. Do not pre-run the predictably over-budget 4,097 case on unchanged source.
3. **Make accepted writes scale.** Replace routine full-record cleanup polling with work-triggered reclaim candidates while preserving quota-pressure/scoped cleanup, ownership, unknown-outcome custody and bounded memory. Then reduce whichever per-write backing operations the API diagnostic shows dominate. Start with existing-format measures such as safe handle reuse or coalescing ownership work within one atomic publication; change to packed page storage only if the measured budget still requires it. Keep read-your-writes and one atomic local-root publication per accepted mutation. Target path-local `O(log P)` extent work and no scan of all earlier writes' retained records.
4. **Finish Commit scaling on the existing route.** Keep `SaveFile` and its bounded service spool. Make ordered extent/descriptor/replacement walks monotone with amortized `O(H+P)` page visits per pass, and release the Workspace mutation gate during `O(P)`, `O(R)` and `O(S)` Commit work. Count C1 mapping visits and deferred bytes at increasing final-run counts. Replace per-run split/concat only if those counts or the API Commit gate show it is necessary, while preserving the exact canonical root and mapping partition for previously accepted inputs.
5. **Prove correctness, then run the gate once at a frozen source identity.** Cover 249/250-leaf transitions, a focused >65,535-run sequence, overwrite/adjacent/no-op/zero/deletion cases, malformed input, two incremental heads and a write accepted during each relevant Commit phase. After focused checks pass and the source, driver, fixture, cache contract and budget are sealed, take one 4,097-run public API attempt per source/arm. That same receipt records Exec and complete functional wall against the harness budgets and, only if cache-qualified, the registered performance gate; keep failures and cleanup evidence. Run the independent verifier once at matching identities. A smaller matched API baseline may be registered before implementation for a speed comparison; native timings are never its control. Diagnose any miss from the receipt and count-driven evidence, change source, then evaluate that new source identity without resampling an unchanged arm.

**Sequence:** implement this follow-up only after package E and the package F candidate arm. The [E/F final report](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/docs/issues/245/evidence/phase1-e-f-final/REPORT.md) records both complete at `ff3dbcfe0`; start from the accepted post-E/F source and keep their receipts unchanged. This is a separate file-delta scope, not a rerun of F or a claim that its cache-ineligible latency cells passed.

## Why

Package D removed the 256-descriptor Begin-frame and 8 MiB replay ceilings, but one existing file still hits a **4,096 final changed-run ceiling** during Workspace writes/lowering, Bridge validation, or C1 construction. The limit is an implementation budget for materialized descriptors, not a property of a file or a requirement to checkpoint each write. It conflicts with [#245's target](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/docs/issues/245/ARCHITECTURE.md#bounds-speed-target-and-limits-of-the-claim) to avoid a fixed changed-interval count.

The Workspace already keeps a live, path-copied `Base` / `Local` / `Zero` **final extent sequence** so accepted writes are readable. Commit derives aggregate changed runs from one frozen version; it does not need the history of shell calls:

```text
base:          a b c d e f g h
shell writes:    b->X, b->Y, c->Z, g->Q   (4 WRITE calls)
final file:    a Y Z d e f Q h
final delta:    [b,c -> Y,Z] [g -> Q]      (2 changed runs)
```

Today the aggregate still becomes several count-sized allocations and C1 applies each *final run* through private split/concat work:

```text
live final extent tree
  +-- write-time Fold.edits / inode u16 count ------> 4,096 refusal
  +-- Commit lower_file -> Vec<Edit> -> packed Vec -> 4,096 refusal
                       -> Bridge Begin(count) + body -> 4,096 refusal
                       -> server block + edits + starts Vecs
                       -> C1 EditStream Vec -> compare/build -> 4,096 refusal
```

Removing one check or raising the number merely moves the failure. The server and C1 must still validate and replay the final delta without retaining an array proportional to its run count.

## Proposed algorithm: aggregate once per frozen file version

1. **Keep live range COW, not canonical write checkpoints.** Continue path-local `Base` / `Local` / `Zero` updates and their atomic local-root publication for read-your-writes. Do not persist a list of prior WRITE calls or publish a canonical Store file version after each. Remove the edit-run count as a write admission rule and resolve the `u16` inode count / `u16::MAX` sentinel without replacing 4,096 with a larger fixed count. Keep the existing file-length, private-backing, page, and deadline protections.
2. **Freeze and summarize the final state at Commit.** Package E's capture pins G1 while new writes enter G2. An ordered, bounded cursor over G1's extents maintains only `base_cursor`, result-coordinate delta, pending non-Base length, descriptor count, replacement-byte total, and checked length totals. At each next `Base(offset, length)`, close one maximal run replacing `base_cursor..offset` with the pending `Local/Zero` bytes; advance the base cursor. Close a nonempty/deletion tail at EOF. This is the final aggregate, independent of overwritten intermediate values and shell-call count. Validate monotone base ranges, exact coverage, replacement totals, and final length.
3. **Replay the immutable aggregate rather than materializing it.** The current generic `SaveFile` metadata declares extent count and byte totals before the body. First pass computes/validates them; a second cursor emits packed 24-byte descriptors into fixed-size frames; the existing replacement source emits only final `Local/Zero` bytes. Keep the cursors monotone across frame pulls so frames do not repeatedly seek the same tree paths. Cross-check emitted count and totals against pass one. The `u32` declared count may remain for framing with checked arithmetic; it is not a 4,096-run admission rule. All passes belong to Commit's work, including any timed Commit phase.
4. **Validate and replay at the service.** Parse descriptors incrementally with bounded RAM, validate ordering/current-result coordinates/overlap/length and exact EndInput totals, and retain a quota-charged replayable descriptor stream plus the existing bounded replacement spool. C1 can replay both for its comparison and construction passes without descriptor/offset `Vec`s.
5. **Build one final canonical result.** C1 consumes ordered retained base spans and final replacement runs, reuses untouched canonical subtrees by identity, and holds only a bounded tree/CDC frontier. It may do work for each *final* run, but must not publish an intermediate file checkpoint/root per run or retain drafts proportional to the number of past writes. Seal only nodes whose boundaries cannot change, then emit one final file root and preserve one Branch-head publication. Preserve current edit-boundary CDC and exact-root semantics for previously accepted inputs; if a bulk builder would change roots, obtain an explicit versioned identity ruling before shipping it.

```text
shell/POSIX writes --> live final range tree --> freeze G1 --> G2 accepts writes
                                               |
                          pass 1: count + validate final delta
                          pass 2: stream descriptors (fixed buffer)
                          pass 3: stream final Local/Zero bytes
                                               |
                         Bridge frames -> service replay spool
                                               |
                         C1 compare -> final mapping -> one file root
                                               |
                                      one Commit publication
```

## Incremental Commit invariant

For a linear sequence in one Workspace, each successful Commit installs the **immediately preceding Commit's file roots and filesystem root as the next base**. `expected_head` pins that predecessor; a moved external Branch head is a conflict/rebase decision, never permission to diff against a stale ancestor. "Compare against Commit n" means using its authenticated base roots and checking only changed ranges, not reading every byte of Commit n.

```text
C_n:       file root R_n, filesystem root F_n
  |
  +-- G_(n+1): local final extents over R_n
  |       Commit (n+1): aggregate delta(G_(n+1), R_n)
  |                     expected_head = C_n; base = F_n
  |                     --> C_(n+1), file root R_(n+1)
  |
  +-- G_(n+2): writes accepted after G_(n+1) was frozen
          temporary base = captured G_(n+1) file version
          after C_(n+1) succeeds, substitute R_(n+1) as that base
          Commit (n+2): aggregate delta(G_(n+2), R_(n+1))
                        expected_head = C_(n+1)
```

For example, if C_n contains `abcdef`, G_(n+1) changes `b` to `X`, and a later generation changes `e` to `Y`, C_(n+1) is `aXcdef` and the next Commit describes only `e -> Y` against that saved version. It does not resend `b -> X` or replay both generations. Unchanged files retain their prior content IDs. Advance the live base only after a known successful outcome; preserve the frozen root and explicit failure/unknown-outcome custody.

## Concurrency boundary

The mounted filesystem can receive operations from multiple processes, and accepted writes after G1 capture belong to G2. Their local publication is atomic; the new delta path must preserve that behavior. **The present public control route admits only one live session (Q=0): two independent `WorkspaceApi::exec` calls, or an `exec` and a `commit` control call, are not concurrently admitted by that daemon.** This issue does not claim otherwise or widen control-session admission. A single shell command may spawn concurrent processes that access the same mount; direct mounted activity can also overlap a Commit once a control call is available. Keep Commit/Stage serialized by the Workspace's one retained submission slot, while FUSE writes proceed in the successor generation. Independent concurrent SDK `exec` calls require their own control-lane work and proof.

Let `P` be extents in the frozen final sequence, `R` its final changed runs, `S` actual replacement bytes, and `H` bounded tree height. The count/descriptor walks visit `O(P)` extents each; instrument page visits so repeated frame pulls do not multiply that traversal by `H`. Wire and temporary spool space cost `O(24R + S)` **actual input bytes**. Resident memory should depend on `H`, page/CDC windows, and fixed I/O buffers, **not `R` or the number of earlier WRITE calls**. Dense final fragmentation necessarily costs at least `Ω(R)` descriptor/output work; target construction proportional to visited mapping nodes, `R`, and changed bytes, without repeated whole-base work. A sparse delta should reuse untouched base payload and mapping subtrees. Keep a declared stream-byte/disk budget and precise `Capacity`/deadline failure; do not disguise a count ceiling inside `input_length <= MAX_FILE` (which currently includes descriptor bytes).

## Acceptance

- A file with **4,097 separated final runs** passes the genuine Workspace → Bridge → service → C1 save path and exact-byte/readback oracle; its previous head remains readable. A focused sequence test also exercises **more than 65,535** runs so the `u16` count does not become the next cap. Do not inflate the existing mounted route's 60 s budget to force a 4,097-WRITE setup to fit; record any unrun mounted cell honestly.
- Many overwrites of the same range and adjacent changes aggregate by final state, not write count. Cover insertion, deletion, truncation, `Zero` holes, no-op base-root reuse, and current-result coordinate arithmetic.
- Two sequential Commits on the same file prove the second `SaveFile` names the first Commit's saved content root as its base and includes only second-generation changed runs. It still allows brief capture/install ordering points and precise quota, deadline or custody refusal. Independent `WorkspaceApi::exec`/Commit control overlap remains #249's separate daemon requirement.

issues.body:
Parent: #245. Sibling: #248 scales final changed runs **within one file**; #249 widens daemon concurrency. This issue scales the **number of changed files, directories and names in one Workspace generation**. Completing #248 alone does not make a package install/update involving hundreds or thousands of tiny files admissible.

## Current source and failure chain

Source pin: current Core `main` at `a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33` (2026-09-26). The ordinary route is public `WorkspaceApi::exec` → POSIX operations on the FUSE mount → explicit `WorkspaceApi::commit`.

- `State::frontier_bytes` rejects more than **128 dirty identities** or **128 changed names** and ties admission to a **32 KiB inline metadata request** ([source](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/runtime/state.rs#L196)).
- A local directory record stores `count: u16`, rejects `count > 128`, and some binding/tombstone operations rebuild up to 128 names into a `Vec` ([source](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/overlay/directories.rs#L23)).
- Commit lowering materializes directory rows and checks 128 again; `PreparedChanges` owns `Vec`s of directories/inodes, Bridge refuses >128 entries/names and limits the metadata request to 32 KiB ([lowering](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/commit/directories.rs#L18), [contract](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33/core/crates/layerfs-bridge/src/contract/request.rs#L586)).
- The live node table has a **256-entry** ceiling; active handle and directory-cookie ceilings and linear `fresh`/`declared`/node lookups need audit under a many-file workload ([source](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/runtime/state.rs#L14)). C1's current filesystem input also accepts materialized slices and collects touched serials; its ordering budget is real, but its input and peak memory must scale deliberately.
- A fixed page fanout or a **128-entry readdir page** may remain as a bounded batch size. It must not cap the total directory or generation.

Raising one constant moves the refusal downstream. A generation that updates 129 small files can fail even if each file has only one changed byte and #248 has removed the per-file run ceiling.

## Target architecture

```text
BEFORE                                      AFTER
POSIX creates/updates                      POSIX creates/updates
  -> 128 dirty/names admission               -> resource-charged, path-local namespace COW
  -> bounded per-directory name Vec           -> ordered bindings/tombstones; no whole-dir rebuild
  -> freeze G1                                -> freeze immutable G1; G2 remains writable
  -> materialized PreparedChanges Vec         -> bounded cursor over final G1 names/inodes
  -> 32 KiB inline HistoryCommand             -> streamed, validated prepared update
  -> C1 consumes one bounded batch            -> C1 consumes replayable ordered input/spool
  -> one Stage/Commit if admitted              -> one exact filesystem root and Branch head
```

The final namespace change set is derived from the frozen generation, not a log of every shell operation. Keep `expected_head`, authenticated base/root, serial allocation, link counts, deletion/tombstone semantics, old-head readability and known/unknown outcome custody. A successful Commit installs the saved root as the next generation's base; writes accepted during Commit remain in the successor and appear in its later Commit. No intermediate Branch head is published for a batch page.

## Concrete algorithm and bounds

Let `F` be final changed inode identities, `K` final changed directory names, `B` their encoded bytes, and `H` the private page-tree height.

1. **Maintain final live state, not an operation log.** The existing generation-keyed dirty-serial index already records one key per dirty identity, and ordinary create already uses a keyed `candidate.update` for one directory binding. Keep those. Add path-local delete/rebind for the binding and tombstone trees; the current `keep_name`, `drop_entry` and `remove_name` paths collect/rebuild the directory and cannot remain `O(K)` per tiny-file mutation. Each mutation checks actual quota, writes only the touched leaf/ancestors, and atomically swaps the local root. Store wide, checked counts/bytes in a versioned directory record; no 128 or `u16` total-name admission.
2. **Bound the observation cache by ownership, not by files changed.** Index live nodes by serial, reclaim unpinned entries, and charge genuinely pinned kernel lookups/handles to the memory budget. A 256-entry cache ceiling or a linear scan of every prior node cannot replace the dirty-identity ceiling. A bounded readdir page or simultaneous-handle slot remains a page/concurrency limit, never a total-directory limit.
3. **Freeze G1 and stream its final namespace.** Pin its immutable root at a short ordering point; G2 mutations use a new root. Walk G1's dirty serials in serial order and each changed directory's bindings/tombstones in name order with persistent page cursors. Reuse the submission's private saved-result tree for content/metadata roots. An optional first pass computes checked record/byte totals; a second pass emits the same immutable rows in fixed-size frames. Frame size (including 128 rows if convenient) is a transport batch, not a generation cap.
4. **Validate, replay and build once.** The service validates strict ordering, unique serials/names, declared totals, role/link rules and exact EndInput while spooling input under a disk quota. C1 reads replayable ordered cursors from that spool; its current slice inputs and touched-serial `Vec` must become bounded iteration or budgeted external merge where their size grows with `F + K`. Feed the canonical filesystem builder one final state and publish one Stage/Commit result, preserving the old root identity for previously accepted inputs. A 129-row operation must not be split into two Branch commits.

Target local namespace work is `O(H)` touched pages per name/identity mutation, plus its actual payload I/O. Frozen lowering visits `O(F + K)` final records with amortized `O(H + touched leaves)` page visits per ordered cursor; C1 may use bounded external merge passes when it needs a second ordering, but no repeated whole-directory or whole-frontier scan per record. Resident memory is bounded by fixed buffers, tree paths and quota-charged *active pins*; temporary disk is charged by actual final records/bytes and merge runs. Quota or deadline exhaustion remains a precise refusal. These bounds are targets to verify with page-visit, allocation, spool and I/O counters, not measured claims.

## Implementation work

1. **Live namespace:** remove cardinality admission from `frontier_bytes` while retaining checked real memory/disk/deadline budgets. Use the existing keyed private page arena for path-local binding and tombstone insertion/deletion, rather than rescanning/rebuilding a whole directory on each tiny-file operation. Widen or version the directory count/byte representation so 128 and `u16` do not become replacement ceilings. Preserve atomic local-root publication and read-your-writes.
2. **Live caches/accounting:** make ordinary sequential creates/opens/forgets work beyond the 256-node cache and audit `fresh`, `declared`, `unbound`, handles and cookies for hidden count ceilings or cumulative quadratic lookups. Evict only unpinned observations; live handles and kernel lookup references remain valid. Charge simultaneous open handles and directory cursors to actual memory/FD/private-backing budgets; no fixed 128-handle or 1,024-cookie admission may bind while those budgets have room. Keep total files changed independent of live-handle count.
3. **Frozen lowering and wire:** walk dirty serials and directory bindings in stable order with bounded cursors. Replace the 32 KiB inline `PreparedChanges` payload and 128-entry decoders with a checked, replayable streaming form; validate ordering, exact counts/bytes and final EndInput before publication. Use quota-charged temporary backing for input too large for the fixed resident window. Both explicit Stage and ordinary Commit must use the same final-state path.
4. **C1/C5:** build one canonical filesystem result from the prepared stream with bounded resident state and spill/merge where needed. Reuse untouched subtrees, retain one-worker construction, and publish one Stage/Commit outcome. Preserve the exact canonical root for inputs the old ≤128 path accepts. Count C1 touched-serial, mapping and ordering work; avoid a new small fixed record cap.
5. **Performance and consistency:** diagnose per-file SaveFile/metadata round trips, private page operations and namespace lookup costs through the public route. Optimize any measured per-file overhead required for a many-tiny-file Exec and Commit to meet the repository performance gates. #249 removes the whole-Exec product runtime deadline; per-syscall and Commit deadlines remain. Prove G1/G2 reconciliation with hundreds of identities; do not enlarge budgets to pass.

## Acceptance

- Public SDK-only workload: one `WorkspaceApi::exec` runs an ordinary file producer through FUSE to create/update **129 names in one directory**, then a separate case changes **257 files** across directories, and a load-bearing package-tree case changes **1,025 tiny files/names** in one generation. Use closed prepared masters and independent writable copies. Exact full-tree bytes, modes, paths, absences, old-head readback and cleanup are checked by an independent verifier. Record actual FUSE calls and per-phase wall; no direct Workspace/Bridge/C1 mutation calls in the benchmark driver.
- Focused tests cover the next count boundary beyond `u16`, mixed create/rename/delete/recreate/hardlink, pagination across more than 1,024 entries on one live directory handle, one directory with many local bindings and tombstones, more than 128 simultaneous active handles when resources permit, and simultaneous active handles versus total changed files. Genuine quota/disk/deadline exhaustion returns a precise failure without partial Branch publication.
- Two sequential Commits prove the second uses the first saved filesystem root and includes only second-generation namespace changes. A mounted write accepted during G1's Commit is visible in G2 and saved by the next Commit.
- Demonstrate path-local live updates (target `O(log M)` touched namespace pages per mutation) and bounded ordered Commit traversal, with resident memory determined by declared buffers/tree height rather than total changed identities. Report actual spool high-water, page visits, lookup work, C1 ordering work, private disk and file-backed cache. Record Exec wall under the repository complete-command/cache rules; one registered sample per case/arm, no benchmark timeout/worker/quota inflation. #249 removes the fixed whole-Exec product runtime maximum.

Implementation can progress alongside #248. Its final many-file performance admission should use #248's improved write path. #245 cannot claim package-install/update scale until both file-run and namespace-cardinality gates pass.

## Load-bearing namespace review — 2026-09-26

The [post-#252 case review](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/codex/issue245-joint-tree-research/core/docs/issues/245/LOAD_BEARING_CASE_REVIEW.md) found a further namespace count gate: C1's `MAXIMUM_WALK_ENTRIES=4,096` reachability/cycle validation can refuse a wide base-directory rebind before configured resources are exhausted ([source](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/f74dbe77da12fa533587be8a578375bce3f19373/core/crates/layerfs-content/src/filesystem/limits.rs#L86)). #256 must replace this fixed visited-binding admission with resource-charged checked traversal and prove a public wide-base-tree operation across that boundary. Removing the Workspace 128-name checks alone does not qualify the many-package/remove-and-copy cases.

A **base-resident directory move** is a separate semantic gap, tracked in sibling [#258](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/258): current `moved_identity` returns `Unsupported` because inherited descendants resolve by old canonical paths. A fresh-upper directory move is not proof for that case. Keep #256's count/streaming proof and #258's origin/identity proof distinct.

issues.title: Post-#248: concurrent Exec and multiple Workspaces per sandbox with serialized Commit
issues.body:
Parent: #245. **Blocked by #248:** begin this implementation and its qualification only after #248's limit-free, Commit-time final-delta path has passed its exact-root, >4,096-run, bounded-memory, and failure-custody gates. Reuse those receipts as evidence; do not rerun or relabel a benchmark arm to make this issue pass. This is the concurrency validation and daemon enablement that follows #248, not a rewrite of package E/F or #248.

**Owner ruling (2026-09-26):** Remove the fixed 30-second *whole-shell* `WorkspaceApi::exec` deadline. An admitted command runs until its process group exits or its caller explicitly cancels, disconnects, or the Workspace/daemon shuts down. Elapsed wall time alone must not kill it. Keep bounded output capture, resource admission, per-FUSE-syscall deadlines, Commit deadlines, and repository benchmark timing gates distinct from this command-lifetime policy. Current SDK, Bridge, native transport, and daemon all enforce the 30-second deadline, so changing one constant is insufficient.

## Goal

One sandbox daemon owns **multiple simultaneously mounted Workspaces** against its configured Store. Each Workspace admits **multiple independent, concurrent `WorkspaceApi::exec` calls** running arbitrary `/bin/sh -c` commands. There is no fixed per-daemon, per-Workspace or lifetime Exec-command count: admitted commands consume actual PID, FD, memory and output resources, and finished leases are released. No scan or retained record of all earlier Exec calls is part of admission. The **only logical serialization rule** is **one Commit/Stage submission at a time per Workspace**. Different Workspaces may Commit concurrently when the Store resource budget admits them; there is no daemon-wide Commit mutex. A Commit freezes G1 while accepted mounted writes enter G2, and the next Commit uses the preceding saved head as its base. Commands are concurrent processes, not whole-command transactions: a shell command's syscalls may straddle a capture boundary.

```text
one sandbox daemon, resource-admitted control sessions
  |
  +-- workspace A (id + incarnation, mount A)
  |     exec A1 ---------+
  |     exec A2 ---------+--> concurrent FUSE operations, atomic local publication
  |     Commit A: one G1 capture/Branch publication; later writes go to G2
  |     second Commit A: refused while A's submission remains
  |
  +-- workspace B (different id + incarnation, mount B)
        exec B1 ---------------------> independent mount and command output
        Commit B: own submission; shared Store writer budget still applies
```

## Why the current source cannot do this

- `WorkspaceHost` already has a charged attachment registry and per-ID mount/backing paths, and the SDK owner records multiple Workspace bindings. The sandbox launcher currently sets `LAYERFS_WORKSPACE_MAX_COUNT=2`. But the daemon lifecycle owns only one `selected` Workspace and one `MountHandle`; a second live mount is not exposed. Sibling #219 owns the operator-facing `max_workspaces_per_sandbox` creation policy. The daemon creates Workspaces internally through `WorkspaceHost::attach`; #249 replaces its singleton lifecycle without inventing another Workspace-count knob.
- The daemon admits one control session (Q=0), and dispatch holds its single lifecycle mutex through the complete `exec` process or Commit. A second independent SDK `exec`, or an `exec` plus Commit, therefore cannot enter concurrently. A shell's own child processes can already overlap through one mount, but that is not concurrent `WorkspaceApi::exec` support.
- The shared Workspace host has one `frozen` admission flag, one remote-operation gate, one metadata writer gate, and one outbound service-session mutex. Several filesystem paths still use immediate `writer()` refusal, surfaced to POSIX as `EBUSY`. These are real contention/forward-progress limits even after opening control sessions.
- Process, mount, and failure custody currently rely on single-owner exclusion. Merely changing the session count could let unmount/shutdown discard an active command or a retained Commit outcome.

## Implementation shape

1. Replace the daemon's singleton selected/mount slot with a bounded registry keyed by **Workspace ID + incarnation**. Each entry owns its native Workspace, mount handle, lifecycle state, active-command leases, and failure custody. Authenticate and resolve the exact entry under a short registry lock; release that lock before shell execution, Store I/O, Commit, or unmount waits. An unrelated Workspace must not be excluded by another entry's long command.
2. Admit authenticated control connections and Exec leases by actual PID, FD and memory availability, with no fixed numeric Exec limit per daemon, Workspace or lifetime. Use one event-driven command supervisor (or a small fixed set shared by all commands) for sockets, nonblocking stdout/stderr pipes and child-exit notification; do not allocate a dedicated OS thread, 2 MiB stack or periodic polling loop for each Exec. Each active Exec owns only a small keyed lease, one process group, its required FDs, bounded output buffers, request/response identity and cleanup state: `O(Q)` charged live state for `Q` active commands, with `O(1)` admission/retirement and no work proportional to completed commands. Let OS process creation and sandbox quotas return precise resource refusal; do not replace a count cap with a hidden queue or automatic replay. Preserve per-Workspace authorization and exact incarnation checks.
3. Keep the **per-Workspace submission slot** as Commit/Stage serialization. A second same-Workspace Commit refuses `Busy` while the first is retained; no duplicate C5 publication. Different Workspaces may make progress concurrently, subject to the Store's existing writer budget and Branch expected-head checks. Move a shared host-wide `frozen`/remote gate only where its scope incorrectly blocks this contract; do not raise construction workers or Store quotas to conceal contention. For two Workspaces targeting one Branch, a moved head is an explicit conflict, never a silent merge or retry.
4. Audit mounted operations for short `writer()` collisions under two commands. Wait only within each FUSE callback's own deadline for ordinary short gate holds; retain precise `Busy` for actual unavailable ownership and preserve per-syscall atomicity. The shell itself has no elapsed-time deadline. In particular, create/rename/remove/write and read paths must not turn routine parallel commands into unexplained `EBUSY`.
5. Unmount/close of one Workspace must refuse or wait while its commands, FUSE callbacks, or Commit own it; other Workspaces remain available. Daemon shutdown retains every incomplete mount/process/Commit owner and reports a bounded failure rather than dropping or guessing custody. Keep the existing 4 GiB file, backing, session/output, and Store budgets; this work adds no whole-shell atomicity guarantee or multi-Store routing.

## Deadline-free Exec implementation

- Make the Exec wire request explicitly distinguish **no total execution deadline** from the finite deadlines required by other operations. Update `Request` validation, SDK `control_call`, native client/server transport, daemon dispatch, and shell execution together; do not substitute a very large finite deadline.
- The current daemon checks elapsed time and sends `SIGKILL` to the process group at the 30-second limit. Remove only that whole-command timer. Preserve a process-group owner from spawn through exit and pipe draining, and terminate/reap on explicit cancellation, client disconnect, Workspace teardown, or daemon shutdown. Define the terminal result for each case; never abandon a running child.
- Keep authenticated transport liveness without a total runtime timer. Send bounded-rate heartbeats even when a command writes no files or output. Progress frames must not consume a small lifetime response-frame allowance (currently `frame_budget(0)`), and a blocked/broken connection must be detected and cleaned up. No unbounded resident output or thread/session growth.
- Retain per-FUSE-callback time bounds, Commit deadlines, configured resource quotas, and repository benchmark wall-time gates. Benchmark timing measures and classifies a run; it does not become the product's shell-kill policy. Verify an Exec can exceed the old 30-second boundary without termination and that cancellation/disconnect/teardown still reap the exact process group.

**Resource admission:** Multiple mounted Workspaces and commands are supported in one sandbox. Exec has no fixed count per daemon, Workspace or lifetime; only actual process/FD/memory availability can refuse a new command. Do not introduce a singleton Workspace, global Commit lock, per-Exec worker thread, or a hidden fixed session/handle/cookie/root/arena count below the selected resource policy. Charge live owners to memory, PID, FD, private-backing and Store budgets; reclaim only after their last owner releases. Sibling #219 owns `max_workspaces_per_sandbox`, which caps internally created live Workspaces only, never Exec calls. Its selected value must admit multiple Workspaces for this issue's proof; the launcher's current `2` is not an architectural maximum.

## Post-#248 validation

- Two distinct Workspaces mount simultaneously in one sandbox; independent paths, content roots, commands, status, unmount, and close are correct. A failed/retained attachment consumes capacity until its exact resources are released. Check the selected #219 count policy without a lower hidden singleton cap.
- Two `WorkspaceApi::exec` calls on the **same** Workspace overlap at a deterministic barrier and both return their own exact exit status/stdout/stderr. Another Workspace's command progresses while either is active. With enough resource headroom, increase concurrent calls beyond two on one and several Workspaces; neither daemon nor Workspace has a fixed Exec-count refusal. Run many sequential completed Exec calls and show prompt lease reclamation, bounded resident memory, no cumulative lookup/cleanup scan and no per-command supervisor thread. Record PID/FD/memory and output high-water plus admission/exit cost. Include disjoint writes and a conflicting-path case with explicit per-syscall ordering; do not claim an entire shell command is atomic.
- While one Workspace has overlapping commands, Commit captures G1, later accepted writes remain in G2, and a second sequential Commit publishes only G2 against the first saved head. Run this on the post-#248 final-delta path, with old-head readback and exact bytes/root. A simultaneous second Commit on the same Workspace is refused without a second publication. With Store writer capacity for two, Commits in two different Workspaces overlap and retain distinct outcomes; a shared Branch head conflict is explicit. Shared Store resource refusals are identified as such.
- A short metadata-gate collision in ordinary namespace/file operations does not produce unexplained `EBUSY`; deadline and true capacity refusals remain exact. Report accepted/rejected command and Commit counts, active process/session high-water, mount ownership, and shared Store admission.
- Unmount/close/shutdown during active commands or a retained Commit has deterministic custody: no orphaned child, lost mount, duplicate operation, leaked Workspace binding, or cross-Workspace teardown. Wrong ID/incarnation and unauthorized control requests cannot reach another Workspace.

**Source anchors:** [daemon singleton lifecycle](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-daemon/src/lifecycle.rs), [Q=0 control and long dispatch lock](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-daemon/src/control.rs), [shell process ownership](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-daemon/src/execution.rs), [Workspace host registry and shared gates](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/runtime/host.rs), [capture/submission slot](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/overlay/snapshot.rs), [sandbox launch count](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-sandbox/src/docker.rs), [#219 workspace-count policy](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/219).

## Source-audited concurrency and resource model — 2026-09-26

The [architecture/complexity research](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7939c56d1/core/docs/issues/245/ARCHITECTURE_COMPLEXITY_RESEARCH.md) at [`7939c56d1`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/commit/7939c56d1) is reviewable in [PR #250](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/pull/250). #249 remains blocked by #248.

At source `74ac30e28`, `WorkspaceHost` has bounded per-ID backing and mount paths, but the daemon still has one selected mount, Q=0 control admission, and a lifecycle lock held through Exec/Commit. FUSE callbacks within one shell can overlap; two independent `WorkspaceApi::exec` calls through the daemon cannot yet overlap. Native `active_operations` counts guarded syscalls and Commit operations, **not a shell between syscalls**. Once the long daemon lock is released, each Workspace needs a command lease from admission before spawn through process-group and output cleanup; unmount/close/shutdown must consult it along with retained Commit custody.

For `V` mounted Workspaces and `Q` admitted commands, target owner state is `O(V+Q)`, plus shell/child RSS, mount threads/FDs, and private pages/payloads. Captured stdout/stderr is currently bounded at 8 KiB each per command; the sandbox's 2 CPU, 512 MiB and 64 PID caps do not prove algorithmic memory or independent throughput. Different Workspaces may still contend on the host-wide remote/metadata gates, outbound transport, Store writer budget, and Branch expected-head checks. Keep one Commit/Stage submission per Workspace and test true two-Exec overlap, an unrelated Workspace, Exec+Commit capture/reconcile, exact response ownership, gate collision, and teardown under active leases with deterministic barriers.

issues.body:
Parent: #245. Sibling: [#249](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/249).

## Goal

Expose one operator-configurable `max_workspaces_per_sandbox` setting. It determines the maximum number of **live Workspace instances that one sandbox daemon may create internally**. `WorkspaceApi::open` asks the daemon to create/attach a Workspace; the caller does not supply a second count or allocate that Workspace outside the daemon. The configured value is admission policy for Workspace creation, not a limit on Exec commands or a global Commit lock. #249 provides the multi-Workspace daemon registry and concurrent command delivery.

A frozen generation and its live successor are one Workspace. Different sandboxes have independent counts. Workspaces created and fully torn down sequentially do not consume a lifetime creation counter.

## Current source

The sandbox launcher currently passes `LAYERFS_WORKSPACE_MAX_COUNT=2`. `WorkspaceHost::attach` checks `WorkspaceConfig.max_count` with a charged registry, but the daemon lifecycle still has only one `selected` Workspace and mount. There is no completed operator-facing setting, and raising the internal host count alone cannot mount a second Workspace.

Source: [sandbox launcher](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/f74dbe77da12fa533587be8a578375bce3f19373/core/crates/layerfs-sandbox/src/docker.rs#L208), [daemon lifecycle](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/f74dbe77da12fa533587be8a578375bce3f19373/core/crates/layerfs-daemon/src/lifecycle.rs#L18), [host admission](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/f74dbe77da12fa533587be8a578375bce3f19373/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/runtime/host.rs#L233).

## Implementation contract

1. Select one positive integer in the operator's sandbox creation profile and pass it unchanged into the daemon's immutable per-sandbox configuration. Keep the current internal value `2` as the proposed default unless the operator selects another value; reject zero and invalid encodings before launch. A running sandbox keeps its selected value for its lifetime; changing it requires a new sandbox, so there is no second live reconfiguration protocol.
2. At the daemon's internal create/attach boundary, reserve one Workspace slot before making its ID/incarnation visible. Use one authoritative count across attaching, attached, mounted, failed-but-retained and closing states. Pass the same selected value to `WorkspaceHost` for charged backing admission; do not leave a hidden singleton or lower hard-coded `2` beneath a larger operator setting.
3. Release a slot only after the exact Workspace, mount and backing owners are fully cleaned up. A failed/unknown attach or incomplete teardown keeps its slot. Count each Workspace once regardless of generations, open handles, commands or frozen Commit roots.
4. On a full sandbox, refuse the next creation precisely without partial visibility. Continue admitting Exec on existing Workspaces according to #249's actual PID/FD/memory resources. This setting never caps concurrent or cumulative `WorkspaceApi::exec` calls. The only Commit serialization remains one active submission per Workspace.

## Acceptance

- With configured values `1`, `2` and `3`, create exactly that many simultaneous Workspaces in one sandbox, refuse the next, then release one and admit a replacement. A value of `3` proves no hidden daemon/host ceiling of one or two. Separate sandboxes enforce their own selected values.
- Include attaching, retained failure and incomplete teardown in the count; a frozen G1/live G2 pair counts once. Verify exact ID/incarnation isolation and that refusal creates no partial mount or backing owner.
- With value at least `2`, sibling #249 proves two mounted Workspaces, overlapping Exec commands and independent per-Workspace Commit slots. Exec commands do not alter this Workspace count; many sequential Workspace creations after clean teardown do not hit a lifetime count.
- Record selected value, live/reserved high-water and each precise capacity refusal. No benchmark timing result is implied by this configuration proof.

issues.title: FUSE mount surface: callback interruption, crash-safe unmount and a zeroed statfs
issues.body:
Parent: #245 (the mounted route is the product surface). Related: #249 (command lease and the whole-Exec timer), #70 (FUSE request count and local callback cost), #69 (durability and fsync semantics — **not** this issue), #256 (the 1,024-entry cookie table), #258 (base-resident directory `mv` refusal).

Source pin: `7a81213ba` (lane head `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation`). Line links are to that commit; the FUSE crate is unchanged by the in-flight 3.4 work.

## The mount surface is closed and mostly good practice — these are the gaps in it

The adapter negotiates a tight, fail-closed envelope: `init` sets `max_write`/`max_readahead` = 128 KiB, `max_background = 1`, `congestion_threshold = 1`, and returns an error if any of them cannot be set ([adapter.rs:113](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L113)); every regular open uses `FOPEN_DIRECT_IO`; the mount options are `RO`/`RW`, `NoSuid`, `NoDev`, `DefaultPermissions`, `Exec`, `NoAtime`, `max_read=131072` with `SessionACL::Owner` and two session threads ([mount.rs:208](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/mount.rs#L208)). Unimplemented operations answer `EOPNOTSUPP`/`ENOSYS`, never a silent success. Three things are nevertheless open, and one of them is user-visible in any interactive shell.

## Gap 1 — an in-flight callback cannot be cancelled (no interrupt handling)

- The adapter handles no `FUSE_INTERRUPT`: there is no `interrupted` reference in `layerfs-fuse`, and `fuser` 0.18 (the pinned version) exposes **no** `Filesystem::interrupt` method at all, so the workspace is never told that a caller was interrupted.
- The only bound on a started callback is `CALLBACK_BUDGET = 10 s` ([adapter.rs:21](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L21)), which the mount documents as "deadline observation points, not preemption" ([mount.rs:136](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/mount.rs#L136)).
- Consequence to be **measured, not assumed**: what a caller sees when it interrupts a blocked callback (e.g. Ctrl-C on a slow `ls`/`cp`), and whether the interrupted mutation is still published afterwards. A mutation that lands after its caller was told the operation was interrupted is a correctness question for the product contract, not only a latency question.

What a fix requires: cancellation, not a bigger timeout. Because third-party crates may not be patched or vendored, the legitimate routes are (a) own the low-level session reader in-crate instead of relying on `fuser`'s dispatch, or (b) record the bounded-step behaviour as the accepted contract with its exact observable shape. This issue is for deciding that with evidence; it is not a licence to raise `CALLBACK_BUDGET` or to special-case a command.

## Gap 2 — no crash-safe unmount

- No `MountOption::AutoUnmount` is requested, and the mount is owned by a session thread inside the daemon ([mount.rs:230](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/mount.rs#L230)).
- If that process is killed hard (`kill -9`, OOM kill, container stop), the mount is left with no server: users of the mount point can block in the kernel until someone unmounts it by hand. Every FUSE filesystem has this hazard; here it is unstated and untested.
- Expected: an explicit statement of what a dead daemon leaves behind and how it is recovered (unmount command, lease/`reserve_mount` behaviour, whether a later attach can reclaim the path), or `AutoUnmount` plus a test that death is observed. Custody of unknown Commit outcomes is a different layer and is already covered by the Workspace contract.

## Gap 3 — `statfs` reports zeros

- `statfs` answers `reply.statfs(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4096, 255, 4096)` ([adapter.rs:400](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L400)) — block size and name length are real, the totals and free counts are zero.
- Consequence: `df` shows an empty filesystem, and any tool that checks free space before writing (package installers, `rsync --preallocate`, some build systems) may refuse for the wrong reason or misreport capacity. The Workspace already carries a configured `disk_budget_bytes`, so a truthful figure exists to report.
- Expected: report the declared budget (or document why zeros are the contract and what tools must not infer from them).

## What is deliberate and must not be "fixed"

Recording these so a later agent does not undo them: direct I/O on every open (no page-cache coherence problem), `max_background = 1` (bounded, chargeable steps), `TTL = ZERO` ([adapter.rs:22](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L22)), `fsync`/`fsyncdir` → `EOPNOTSUPP` ([adapter.rs:407](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L407)), `getxattr`/`listxattr`/`readdirplus` → `EOPNOTSUPP`, `setxattr`/`removexattr` → `EOPNOTSUPP` on a writable mount and `EROFS` on a read-only one ([adapter.rs:69](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L69)), `RENAME_EXCHANGE`/`RENAME_WHITEOUT` → `EINVAL`, a single write over 128 KiB → `E2BIG` ([adapter.rs:539](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7a81213ba/core/crates/layerfs-fuse/src/adapter.rs#L539)), regular files only in `mknod`. Each is a declared boundary with continuation or an explicit refusal; none is a bug.

## Acceptance

1. **Interrupt case.** With a callback deliberately held (a slow operation on the mounted tree), signal the caller and record exactly: the syscall's return, whether the callback completed, whether the mutation was published, and the elapsed time. Then state the contract: cancellation, or a bounded step with the observable shape documented. Repeat for a read, a write and a rename, since the three take different paths. Report `EINTR`/timeout outcomes and the published state; do not claim "interrupt works" from one path.
2. **Daemon-death case.** Kill the serving process while a mount is live; record what a subsequent `stat`, `ls` and `df` on the mount point do, how long they block, and the exact recovery command. If the answer is `AutoUnmount`, assert the mount point is gone within a bounded time and that a later attach can reclaim the path.
3. **`statfs` case.** Compare `df` and `statvfs` output against the configured `disk_budget_bytes`, for an empty workspace and after writes, and assert the numbers are truthful or that the zeros are documented with the tool consequences.
4. **Refusal table case.** One mounted case per refused operation asserting the documented errno (`fsync`, `getxattr`, `setxattr`, oversize write, `RENAME_EXCHANGE`, `mknod` of a FIFO), so the envelope cannot drift into a silent success. The FUSE callbacks are exercised today only below the mount, so this needs a real mount: use the recorded container recipe (`rust:1.85.1-bookworm`, `layerfs-i245-phase1`) or an equivalent Linux ext4 volume.

No performance or POSIX-conformance claim is made or implied by this issue. A conformance run (`pjdfstest`/LTP/`fsx` — currently referenced only inside the peer study under `docs/roadmap/0.1/0.1.7/study/drive9/`) and a crash/`kill -9` stress case would each need their own issue; `fsync` durability semantics stay with #69, FUSE request counts with #70, the base-resident directory `mv` refusal with #258, and the listing cookie table with #256.

issues.title: Diagnose and optimize 4,097 mounted writes through WorkspaceApi::exec
issues.body:
Parent: #248 (under #245). Related dependency: #249 removes the current whole-Exec product deadline.

## Goal

Diagnose and optimize 4,097 separated one-byte writes to an existing file through the **public** `WorkspaceApi::mount` → one `WorkspaceApi::exec` → one `WorkspaceApi::commit` route. The Exec command must perform ordinary positional file writes on the mounted FUSE Workspace. No benchmark driver may call `Workspace::own_payload`, `Workspace::write_file`, FUSE callbacks, Bridge, Service, C1, or Store mutation methods to create the workload. Product code must not recognize the benchmark command or use a special route.

This issue owns **public write-path cost attribution and the smallest justified speed fixes**. #248 retains final-delta/Commit semantics and the full 4,097-run public acceptance gate; this issue supplies its measured Exec-side diagnosis and performance repair.

## Known evidence and open question

The #252 native Workspace frontier timed out at its original 60 s functional wall before 4,097 writes completed. Its count diagnostic reached 512 writes in 14.7 s, 1,024 in 32.6 s, and 1,536 in 53.5 s. A phase diagnostic attributed 33.7 s to payload acquisition and 19.2 s to publication by write 1,536, but a separate shared-payload diagnostic still took about 54 s to reach 1,536 writes. These are historical native-method diagnostics, **not** SDK Exec/FUSE performance samples or a current-source causal proof. The changed-source 1,024 native Workspace proof completed in 40.715 s. See [#252 report](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/a72d07ef81794f1a7224eb721c8673e503cfcb33/core/docs/issues/252/REPORT.md) and its linked append-only receipts. The focused 4,097 in-memory extent test proves path-local tree traversal only; it does not measure private backing or the mounted route.

Current source has work-triggered payload-reclaim candidates. Do not assume the earlier whole-registry-scan cause still exists. Determine where the current 100-write public path spends its work before selecting a fix.

## First action: one 100-write public diagnostic

1. Read repository/core/benchmark `AGENTS.md` and `docs/general/benchmark_rules.md`. Commit a prospective workload/evidence specification **before** implementing a new runner or taking a sample. Reuse the existing release `benchmark_shell` SDK driver and prepared-master clone mechanics where they fit; keep the host SDK, Store and SQLite on the host, with the Linux daemon/FUSE/writer in the sandbox.
2. Prepare an existing `data.bin` with at least 8,194 known bytes. Put a small release writer executable in the sandbox image outside the mount. Invoke it with one short Exec command such as `/fixtures/bin/write-separated data.bin 100`. It opens the file once and makes exactly 100 one-byte positional write syscalls at offsets `2*i`, `i=0..99`; it does not launch one shell or `dd` process per write. Then invoke one explicit SDK Commit. The same writer accepts a declared count for a later 4,097 case; no product hook is added.
3. Record one labelled **diagnostic** at 100 writes, not a speed admission sample. Retain source/tree, release binary, image, fixture, command, cache state, complete wall, Exec wall, Commit wall, cleanup, exit status, old/new-head bytes, failures and every unrun row. Keep verification outside the performance timer. The complete selected command must obey the repository's 15 s budget, or a prospectively declared 25 s exception; a miss stays a miss. Each focused test command must finish under 30 s. Do not increase the workload or deadline to obtain a pass.
4. Capture count-driven progress within those 100 writes (for example cumulative counts at 25/50/75/100) without a status RPC or output write for every mutation. Treat any instrumentation overhead as diagnostic. Independently verify that the old head is unchanged, the new file has exactly 100 separated changed runs and the expected bytes, and cleanup is complete. Count actual FUSE WRITE callbacks; do not infer callback count from the 100 syscalls.

## Required diagnosis and analysis

| Layer | Count and explain |
| --- | --- |
| Public/daemon round trips | SDK mount/Exec/Commit calls, control frames, shell/writer process launches, progress/status polls, output frames, and any unexpected per-write RPC. One Exec and one Commit are the intended public call counts. |
| FUSE and kernel | Writer syscalls and bytes; actual FUSE LOOKUP/OPEN/WRITE/FLUSH/RELEASE/GETATTR/READ callbacks, sizes and elapsed cost; identify writeback, splitting or extra callbacks rather than assuming one callback per syscall. |
| Payload and private backing | Payload acquisitions, segment file create/allocate/write/close calls, actual allocated bytes, retained owners, routine-reclaim candidates/scans, ownership-ledger reads/writes and lock/wait time. Separate fixed per-write cost from work that grows with earlier writes. |
| Extent/page index | Before/after extent count, B+ tree fanout/height, page reads/writes/allocations/reuse per splice, root publication, path-copy and split work, and page/ledger I/O amplification. Distinguish the file extent index from namespace and canonical C1 trees. |
| Commit/Store | Frozen cursor page visits and reseeks, final descriptors/replacement bytes, Bridge/Service round trips, C1 node visits, Store writes/transactions and one head publication. Keep Commit time separate from the 100-write Exec time. |

Produce a source-grounded cost model with `N` accepted writes, `E` live extents, `H` extent-tree height, `R` final changed runs and `S` final replacement bytes. For this workload, `E` and `R` grow with `N`. The intended per-write index work is `O(H + touched)` with no scan proportional to prior writes; total accepted-write work should be `O(N log E)` plus real `O(N)` callback/payload/ledger I/O. Commit should traverse the final state with bounded cursors, rather than replay historical writes. State any measured or source-derived deviation, its exact loop/call site and counts. One 100-write elapsed number alone is insufficient to infer a growth order: use within-run count slopes and, only if needed, separately declared count-driven diagnostics at distinct sizes. Do not resample an unchanged arm for a better time.

Use a subagent for an **independent** source audit of complexity, control/FUSE round trips and extent B+ tree page/index behavior. The primary session owns the 100-write public diagnostic and integrates the subagent's findings. Resolve disagreements from code and retained counts before changing the algorithm.

## Implementation and completion

- Fix the demonstrated shared root cause with the smallest product change; do not add a second mutation route, benchmark-only product branches, test-only hooks, new dependencies, or a speculative packed-page format. Keep atomic read-your-writes, resource charging, G1/G2 ownership and exact canonical Commit results. Update affected Core architecture docs with algorithm/limit changes and record exact production LOC before/after/delta for each commit.
- Use locked release binaries and focused verification. No debug binaries, no test command over 30 s, no rerun of a passing unaffected check, and no repeated performance arm at one identity. Keep append-only FAIL/INELIGIBLE receipts. At final changed source, run the Core checks that cover the change and report gaps precisely.
- After 100-write attribution and fixes, freeze the 4,097 workload, cache contract, source, image, budget and independent verifier. Run the 4,097 public Exec/Commit gate once per prospective source/arm, with exact bytes, old/new heads, actual FUSE counts, resources, Exec/Commit/complete wall and cleanup. #249 owns removal of the current 30 s product Exec timer; do not hide that dependency or raise a harness budget to compensate. The repository performance budget remains separate from product command lifetime. Report any remaining miss and measured cause, rather than calling an unrun or cache-ineligible row a speed PASS.

Coordinate with the concurrent Phase 4/#258 session through a separate worktree. Preserve its changes and the historical #252 receipts.

# Single owner-directed deferred limitations tracker

**Status: deferred, not implemented/qualified.** The owner clarified that all known limitations handed off when closing #265, #266, #270, #271 and #273 belong in **one** issue with the `deferred` label. The provisional #277–#282 were closed as superseded, **not completed**; their bodies/comments preserve the initial split for audit. Gitignored `benchmark-results/fs-bench-pro/issue273/checkpoint5-optimization/iter-012`–`iter-019` are **local** evidence, not GitHub raw URLs.

## 1. SDK same-Workspace pinned journal: owner decision required (former #276)

The public `WorkspaceApi` exports mount/exec/commit/status/unmount but no live same-Workspace G1 journal pin/lease/release spanning the registered clean and one-edit sequential SDK Exec/Commit controls; both currently emit `NOT_RUN`. A detached Store, closed fixture or Workspace-only Stage is not a substitute. **Owner choose one:** prospectively approve a public SDK/Bridge lease specifying selected identity, G1 old-reader bytes, continuing G2 process/edit admission, max 32 captures, charged ownership/refund, cancellation, deadlines and known/unknown canonical custody, with independent byte/pin/failure oracles; **or** explicitly rule/waive these two controls for a named profile while retaining `NOT_RUN` and not calling the 12-row registry complete. No approval or waiver has been recorded. See [decision request](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/9e906331a/core/docs/issues/273/OWNER-RULINGS-SDK-CACHE-CONTROL.md).

## 2. Matched frozen control and private cache/phase-cgroup evidence (former #277)

An owned, clean detached checkout pins frozen #271 product `48b51e874a41b3e1e6c6661e145316df8b408f07` (tree `64d06dabba1a6d123d1002487c189809ded05cc0`) but has **no control samples**. Nine candidate rows pass independent bytes; **all remain numerically INELIGIBLE**. Host source mincore PASS and Linux O_DIRECT request do not prove private container metadata/VM/backend/device/host cache equivalence. An owned Docker cgroup-v2 probe released a 32 MiB shmem file and wrote `0` to writable `memory.peak`; readback still reported **36,163,584** while `memory.current` was **2,428,928**. A lifetime peak cannot be called a phase peak. **Gate:** supply identical verifiable private cache and Exec/Commit-local cgroup conditions for both arms, port only genuinely common observer/harness changes without editing frozen product, then prospectively run all 12 control→candidate rows row-major once per changed identity; or record an owner ruling that numeric comparison remains ineligible on this profile. No censored 25-second control wall as a denominator. See [iter-018](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/9e906331a/core/docs/issues/273/CHECKPOINT5-OPTIMIZATION-LOG.md#iteration-018--explicit-c1-zero-provenance-frozen-control-arranged-numeric-admission-blocked).

## 3. Normalization pages and package-scale C5 limits (former #278/#279)

At the unchanged default 8 MiB Budget the nonregistered 8,192-WRITE functional diagnostic passes full bytes/Commit/clean-close; a distinct 10,240-WRITE control after a known remote Commit locally refuses C5 `Capacity` and retains custody, then ACKs a new G2 WRITE. A **physical** backing allocation fault instead stops writes with `Busy`. None of this proves arbitrarily many edits, multi-file package installs/updates/deletes, clean-close refund after a *retained failed* attempt, or constant RAM. ## Status and scope

**Deferred host/runtime capability observation, not a demonstrated LayerFS product bug, numerical waiver, or release/merge approval.** This narrowly tracks an apparently successful but ineffective cgroup-v2 `memory.peak` reset on the Docker Desktop host. The owner requested a separate deferred issue on 2026-09-29 UTC. The broad matched-cache/phase-cgroup gate remains in #276 §2; earlier #277 was closed as a superseded *broad* duplicate, not as completed work. Keep #276 open.

## Observed (capability-only; no product performance arm)

On macOS arm64 / Docker Desktop Linux `6.12.76-linuxkit`, an observer privileged with `--cgroupns=host` addressed only an owned sandbox container's cgroup. Writing `0` to that container's `memory.peak` returned rc=0, but readback remained **2,798,239,744 bytes** after `memory.current` fell to approximately **30 MB**. An earlier independent owned probe likewise read **36,163,584** peak versus **2,428,928** current after its apparently successful reset. These are distinct probes, not repeated performance samples. A successful write alone is *not* evidence of a reset; the lifetime peak cannot be attributed to Exec or Commit.

As a separate positive observation on the same host, writing `memory.reclaim` to the owned container's cgroup lowered `memory.stat:file` from **808,337,408** to **49,152 bytes** (`memory.current` **884,494,336 → 30,314,496**); a second reclaim was idempotent at that floor. This supports per-container private-cache invalidation, **not** phase-local peak measurement or equal VM/backend/device/host cache identity.
